source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Perform hand hygiene, use aseptic technique and recommended skin antisepsis, then apply a sterile dressing; clean or sterile gloves are acceptable.","B":"Use sterile gloves, but omit skin antisepsis if the previous transparent dressing remained intact.","C":"Use clean technique without aseptic precautions once a central catheter has remained complication-free for several days.","D":"Use maximal sterile barriers with cap, gown, sterile gloves, and full-body drape because routine central-line dressing care should mirror insertion precautions."}}
source_row.rationale: CDC recommends hand hygiene and aseptic technique when dressing an intravascular catheter. For dressing changes, either clean or sterile gloves are acceptable; maximal sterile barrier precautions are required for central-line insertion, not every routine dressing change. The site is disinfected with the recommended antiseptic and covered with a sterile dressing.
